news.title: Norway’s viral World Cup Viking Row has officially made its way into American college football
news.lede: Norway's Viking Row was one of the most viral fan traditions of the 2026 World Cup. Now, two months later, it has officially made its way into American college football. The University of Minnesota debuted its own version of the synchronized rowing chant at its season opener at Huntington Bank Stadium, with the student section sitting in rows and mimicking the same exaggerated rowing motion that Norwegian fans made famous this summer. Former Gophers linebacker Kamal Martin led the chant before kickoff.

news.title: Spanish officials politicize World Cup over Ceuta crisis
news.lede: Spanish political and football circles have once again demonstrated their willingness to weaponize sport for short-term political gain, this time by dragging the July migrant crisis in Ceuta into the debate over the 2030 FIFA World Cup final. Last Friday, Rafael Louzán, president of the Spanish Football Federation (RFEF), travelled to Ceuta accompanied by national team coach Luis de la Fuente. What was presented as a gesture of solidarity quickly turned into a thinly veiled political operation. Louzán used the enclave to push Spain’s claim for the World Cup final while explicitly linking the migrant arrivals of late July to the joint Spain-Portugal-Morocco candidacy.

news.title: World Cup winner Llorente retires from Spain duty at 31
news.lede: World Cup winner Marcos Llorente announced his retirement from international football on Thursday, ending a Spain career that yielded 27 caps. The Atletico Madrid defender, 31, made his senior team debut for Spain in 2020 and was part of the squad that beat Argentina 1-0 to win the World Cup in July, although he remained on the bench in the final. "I realise that I’m still young and that, perhaps, if I continued to perform well, I’d still have years left to play in this jersey," Llorente wrote on Instagram. "I know many of you won’t understand this, and I probably wouldn’t have understood it either if I were looking at it from the outside.
